bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/defaults.rs, springboard/sdk/src/coding.rs, springboard/sdk/src/document.rs, springboard/sdk/src/restoration.rs, springboard/ui/src/undo.rs, springboard/ui/src/diff.rs, springboard/ui/src/fetch.rs, springboard/ui/src/history.rs, springboard/core/src/migrate.rs, springboard/src/shell/contactstore.rs, springboard/src/shell/calendar/store.rs, springboard/core/src/fsutil.rs
summary: BifrOSt has no object graph and no database-backed store. Apps persist their data as small atomically replaced text or JSON files through Codable, UserDefaults and the document layer. Fetch requests with predicates, sort descriptors and paging, a persistent history log and a versioned migration chain now exist as pure models, but no store writes to the history and no store runs its migrations yet. Persistent history across devices, CloudKit mirroring and sharing have no on-device counterpart; sync exists only as server-side counters in bifrost-cloud.

features.note: No managed store abstraction; each app writes its own files in its data directory. No SQLite-backed store.

features.apple: Core Data model editor, NSManagedObjectModel, NSEntityDescription, NSRelationshipDescription (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coredata/modeling-data)
features.note: Codable encodes a value tree per type by hand or with the codable! macro. There is no entity model, no relationships and no inverse tracking.
Apps keep plain Rust structs in memory and rewrite the whole store on save. No faulting, no per-object dirty tracking, no context isolation.

features.apple: NSFetchRequest, NSPredicate, NSSortDescriptor, fetchLimit and fetchOffset (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coredata/nsfetchrequest)
features.note: Comparisons, text containment, and/or/not, stable multi-key sorting, offset and limit work over any record that exposes named fields. Missing: fetch batch size, relationship prefetching, entity names and a store behind the request. Contacts and calendar still filter their own vectors and do not use this model yet.
Work can run off the main loop with dispatch, and the app must do its own store locking. There is no fetch-result object with progress notification.
Diffing turns two identifier lists into insert, remove and move edits. Nothing binds the results of a query to a table automatically, and the app must recompute the list.

features.feature: Undo and redo of model changes
features.apple: NSUndoManager integration with managed object contexts (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coredata/undo-and-redo-of-individual-and-batched-changes)
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/undo.rs (UndoManager<T>, groups, coalesced registration, levels of undo)
features.note: The undo manager is generic over the app's state and does not track model edits. The app must register each undo action itself.

features.apple: Persistent history tracking, NSPersistentHistoryTransaction, NSPersistentHistoryChange, NSPersistentHistoryToken (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coredata/persistent-history)
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/history.rs (History, Token, Transaction, Change, is_complete_since, purge_through), springboard/sdk/src/fswatch.rs (file change notifications, separate)
features.note: A transaction log with bookmarks, incomplete-reader detection and purge exists as a pure model. No store writes to it yet, so saves do not produce transactions. Remote merging of history is missing.

features.apple: Using Core Data in the background, batch processing (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coredata/using-core-data-in-the-background)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/dispatch.rs (serial queues for one store file)
features.note: Serial queues give the single-writer pattern. Batch insert and batch delete over a store do not exist because the store is a file, not a database.
Coordinated file access prevents torn writes between processes. There are no per-object merge policies.

features.feature: Versioned file format and schema versioning
features.apple: Lightweight, staged and manual migrations, NSMigrationManager (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coredata/migrating-your-data-model-automatically)
features.bifrost: springboard/core/src/migrate.rs (Plan, stepwise migrations, refusal of newer data), springboard/src/shell/contactstore.rs (HEADER springboard-contacts-v1), springboard/src/shell/calendar/store.rs (HEADER springboard-calendar-v1), springboard/sdk/src/restoration.rs (foreign or corrupt state ignored)
features.note: A migration chain runs one step per version and refuses data from a newer build. The contacts and calendar stores still reject foreign headers and do not run the chain. No mapping model or staged migration with a custom step over a whole store.

features.apple: NSUserDefaults is outside Core Data; Core Data stores only app records
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/defaults.rs (UserDefaults, typed keys, atomic write per change)
features.note: Typed preference storage with atomic writes covers the small-value case that apps use instead of a store.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/document.rs (document model, recents persistence near line 917)
features.note: Documents save to files and remember recents. Core Data-backed documents with a store and per-object undo are not supported.

features.apple: Core Data integrates with Combine publishers for managed objects (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coredata/nsmanagedobjectcontext)
features.note: Observable values notify subscribers on change. Nothing publishes changes from a store because there is no store.

features.bifrost: none on the device; ~/Projects/bifrost-cloud/docs/schema.md ( sync_cursors, change counters) is server side
features.note: The desktop has no iCloud sync (docs/bifrost-ui.md, iCloud section). Sync is an account service in bifrost-cloud and does not mirror a local store.
Tied to Apple's iCloud accounts. The BifrOSt Account service has no record sharing.

features.apple: Transformable attributes, binary data attributes, NSSecureUnarchiveFromData (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coredata/handling-different-data-types-in-core-data)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/coding.rs (Value::Bytes via JSON and plist encoders)
features.note: Values can be encoded to JSON or XML plist. There are no attribute types in a model, so type checks happen in each app.

gaps: No object graph: no entity model, relationships, inverse relationships or delete rules.
Fetch requests exist as an in-memory model only: no fetch batch size, no relationship prefetching, and no store behind them.
No managed object context with change tracking, dirty state or faulting.
No database-backed store, so stores are rewritten whole on each save and do not scale past the bounded lists (contacts MAX_ITEMS 10000, calendar MAX_EVENTS 2048).
The persistent history model is not written by any store, so no save produces transactions yet, and merging history from another device is missing.
The migration chain is not run by the contacts or calendar stores. Staged and manual migrations over a whole store are missing.
No fetched results controller that binds a query to a table or list.
No on-device CloudKit-style mirroring or sharing; sync exists only as server-side counters in bifrost-cloud.
